idea_headline: The sheet on the wall, made clickable.
idea: Signout is the clipboard sign-out sheet every shared workshop has: kraft paper, a marker-black grid, hazard tape along the top, hatching where someone else has already signed, a stamp when you have. It makes a booking tool feel like a thing you can put your hand on, and it keeps the state honest: open, yours, or taken.
use_for: Booking and reservation apps, intake and sign-up forms, rosters and shift sheets, inventories and loan logs, any tool where people claim slots or things.
avoid_when: Reading-heavy pages, luxury or editorial subjects, dashboards with many simultaneous metrics, or anything that needs to feel soft.
principles: Open is a blank cell. Yours is vermilion. Taken is hatched in ink. No fourth state, no colour for taken: a hatch says it without shouting.
Rows are things, columns are times. The reader picks a cell, not a card. The grid has a 2px ink frame and 1px rules.
Condensed caps in heavy black, like a marker. One vermilion element per view: the pick, the primary button, or the stamp.
A hazard stripe marks what needs reading before acting: a machine with a safety note, a form that will be sent, a slot you are about to release.
A confirmed action lands as a rotated stamp: SIGNED OUT, RETURNED, BOOKED. Stamps are the receipt.
voice: Imperative, short, on the sheet: "Pick a machine. Pick an hour."
Say who and when: "Signed out by R. Okafor, 11:00–11:50."
Label the prototype as a prototype, in the small print on every sheet.
Empty states say what to do, not that there is nothing: "Nothing on the bench. Pick a machine above."
colour_headline: Kraft, marker black, one vermilion, a hazard stripe.
colour_note: Day is the paper: clean kraft with marker-black ink and a hot vermilion pick. Night is the chalkboard: green-black ground, chalk-white ink, the vermilion lifted, the hazard tape unchanged. Taken slots are hatched in ink (or chalk) in both modes; they never take a colour.
chart_note: Charts are marker drawings: ink first, vermilion for the exception, hazard for the warning. Utilisation is better shown as a filled grid than as a bar chart.
type_headline: Barlow Condensed shouts, Barlow explains, JetBrains logs.
type_note: Barlow Condensed at 800 and 700 in caps carries titles, row names and labels. Barlow carries instructions. JetBrains Mono carries ids, times and the shop log.
space: Cell padding on dense sheets; the hatch pitch.
Cell padding on roomy sheets; control padding-y.
edges: Everything. Paper is cut square and tape is straight.
Cells and rows inside the grid.
The taken state. Drawn with clipped lines, never a pattern fill.
depth: None. The sheet is pinned flat. A picked cell is vermilion, not raised.
A 2px vermilion outline, offset 0, inside the cell.
A 2px ink box rotated −10°, Condensed caps inside; lands once (scale 1.15 → 1, 140ms).
Cells change state instantly. The only motion is the stamp landing and the hazard stripe scrolling on a warning (optional, reduced-motion safe).
components_headline: A grid, a stamp, a hatch.
components_note: Kit components take Signout through the contract: kraft grounds, vermilion primary, zero radius, line rules. Authored classes add the sheet frame, the slot cells, the hatch and the stamp.

motifs_headline: Hatching, hazard tape, and a stamp.
motifs_note: Signout draws with what is on the workshop wall. The data lives in the cells: a slot is open, yours or hatched; a warning is tape; a confirmation is a stamp.

motifs.title: The hatch
motifs.usage: 45° ink lines at an 8px pitch, clipped to the cell. It means taken by someone else. Never use a colour for this state; the hatch reads at any size and in both modes.

motifs.title: The hazard stripe
motifs.usage: Yellow and ink chevrons along the top edge of anything that needs reading before acting: a sheet, a warning, a destructive button. 10px tall, never animated by default.

dos: Three states: open blank, yours vermilion, taken hatched.
Frame every sheet in 2px ink and put hazard tape where care is needed.
Condensed caps for titles and labels; plain Barlow for instructions.
Stamp confirmations; log everything with a time.
donts: No colour for the taken state; hatch it.
No rounded corners, shadows or gradients.
No second accent; hazard is a warning, not a brand.
No empty state that says "nothing here" without saying what to do.
binding_losses: The hatch, the hazard stripe, the stamp and the sheet grid have no contract slot; they are so-* classes and inline SVG. Kit tables take the rules and mono figures but not the condensed caps header.
footer: Kraft first, chalkboard second. Fonts: Barlow Condensed 500/700/800 and italic 700, Barlow 400/500/600, JetBrains Mono 400–700, all Google-hosted.

data.tab_body: Sheet: three machines, three slots, one hatched.

hand.headline: A marker, a ruler, and hatching for everything filled.
hand.note: Signout draws the way a sheet on the wall is drawn: 2px marker lines with square caps, no fills except hatching. The pick is hatched in vermilion, the taken parts in ink, and the quiet parts stay kraft. No shadows, no curves that a ruler could not make.
rules: 2px ink, square caps and joins. Every edge is ruled.
None. A filled region is hatched at 45°, 6px pitch: vermilion for the pick, ink for taken.
None. The sheet is pinned flat.
The hatch is the only texture; the hazard chevron is the only ornament.
Condensed caps for the number; mono caps at 11px for labels.
A drawing never moves. A stamp lands on it.

motion: An open cell darkens to kraft-sunk, 100ms linear. Nothing lifts.
Instant. The cell becomes vermilion on release.
A 2px vermilion outline inside the cell.
The one animation: scale 1.15 to 1 in 90ms ease-out, once, then it stays.
None. The sheet is simply there. Reduced motion changes nothing.
The stripe may scroll on a live warning (12px per second); off by default.

tpl.ed_headline: Who had the drill press, and when
tpl.ed_deck: A week on the sign-out sheet: five bookings, one cancellation, and the hour nobody wants. What the shop log says about a shared bench.
tpl.ed_body: The drill press was signed out four times this week and the soldering station once, which is the same shape as every week since the sheet went up. The 10:00 slot goes first; the noon slot goes last. The one cancellation came from a member who booked two machines for the same hour and read the hazard note too late.
steps: A hundred bookings on one sheet.
Each cell is a booking; hatched cells were taken by another member before you looked.
Most of them are the same machine.
The drill press takes the first column. Everything else is open most of the day.
